<h2 id="qa-7404b15170e7203f">Is an MSA history block a new layer or a token-axis candidate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aminimax-sparse-attention">MiniMax Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Blocks organize history for indexing. A light branch chooses blocks and the main branch reads their tokens. Block selection and exact attention have separate costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing a chapter in a table of contents differs from reading its sentences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.13392-minimax-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7404b15170e7203f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:minimax-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="MiniMax Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be7681bf09e68302">What does MSA save and preserve by selecting blocks before exact attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aminimax-sparse-attention">MiniMax Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A cheap block index reduces the historical range; main attention computes exact token interactions inside hits. Summaries select rather than replace tokens. A missed answer block cannot be recovered by exact attention on the rest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose two of ten pages to read word by word, saving main attention on eight but missing a date if its only page was dropped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.13392-minimax-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be7681bf09e68302">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:minimax-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="MiniMax Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b463a148aea8bf76">Does MSA indexing do the same thing as shrinking main attention KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aminimax-sparse-attention">MiniMax Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The index decides where to read; main attention keeps its own exact Q/K/V inside selected blocks. Compressing KV changes what representations are read, not only where.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting two original passages preserves different evidence from summarizing the whole text into two passages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.13392-minimax-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b463a148aea8bf76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:minimax-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="MiniMax Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ce248cccdc3b3a1">Why doesn&#x27;t reduced MSA attention pair ratio imply the same speedup?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aminimax-sparse-attention">MiniMax Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Runtime includes indexing, selection, movement, and kernels. The unfused PyTorch/MPS path has fewer pairs but takes longer. Report pair ratio, PPL, and measured time separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An 80% pair reduction can still slow training if overhead dominates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.13392-minimax-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ce248cccdc3b3a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moba" data-paper-title="MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-moba-f8997c1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-90411b0ae7184500">Why group history into blocks instead of reading all of it for every query?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoba">MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing picks a few relevant blocks, then exact attention reads inside them. This reduces candidate pairs while keeping within-block detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A question needing two passages need not attend to every word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13189">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.13189-moba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90411b0ae7184500">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moba" data-paper-title="MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-627cf3d7c1d91b13">Why keep the current causal block when MoBA routes to a few remote ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoba">MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing finds distant evidence; current-block retention protects nearby context from routing misses. Causal masking restricts visible positions, and attention inside selected blocks is exact at token level. Sparsity does not preserve every distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep the current subject even if remote chapters score higher; do not read the current block&#x27;s ungenerated suffix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13189">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.13189-moba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-627cf3d7c1d91b13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moba" data-paper-title="MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d037963927322859">What can content-routed MoBA recover that a recent window cannot?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoba">MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A window excludes positions by age. Routing can recover relevant distant blocks but can still miss evidence. Cost depends on block size and routing budget; it is not lossless pruning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A name at the beginning can return through content matching instead of being automatically excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13189">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.13189-moba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d037963927322859">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moba" data-paper-title="MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f47a19dd639778f">Does selecting the current MoBA block remove the need for causality inside it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoba">MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Mask positions after the query inside the selected block. The local eight-token, top-two configuration is not a million-context fused kernel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Word three cannot read word seven merely because both share an eight-token block.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13189">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.13189-moba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f47a19dd639778f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mobius-rope" data-paper-title="Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mobius-rope-d829e106" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a35ee6b0b63900fc">What retrieval instability is Möbius RoPE intended to address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amobius-rope">Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Standard RoPE long-range needle retrieval can vary strongly by training seed. Antiperiodic frequencies on some heads aim to stabilize cross-window phase while leaving others unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical needles in long text can produce very different retrieval results across seeds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21405">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21405-mobius-rope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a35ee6b0b63900fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mobius-rope" data-paper-title="Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9cea57bf909d2052">How does Möbius position encoding differ from standard RoPE across a training window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amobius-rope">Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Antiperiodic frequencies on some heads yield −I at one window and I at two. Other heads retain standard RoPE for language modeling. This changes positional geometry, not accessible history or guaranteed retrieval at all lengths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At N positions the selected heads reverse phase; at 2N they realign. Actual retrieval still depends on Q/K and training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21405">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21405-mobius-rope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9cea57bf909d2052">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mobius-rope" data-paper-title="Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7909d719708669df">What explicit frequency boundary does Möbius add?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amobius-rope">Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Set some two-dimensional frequencies to π(2i+1)/N, producing −I across N and I across 2N. Other heads keep standard RoPE. This is geometry, not measured improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reverse phase after one window and recover after two, not arbitrary scaling across every head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21405">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21405-mobius-rope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7909d719708669df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mobius-rope" data-paper-title="Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8f3ab0c1ff95aa5">Should Möbius RoPE change N dynamically with inference length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amobius-rope">Anti-Periodic Positional Encoding: Möbius Boundary Conditions Make In-Context Retrieval Reliable</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. N is fixed training context; local N=64 replaces one of four heads. Dynamic N changes frequencies for identical positions and breaks the boundary definition. Retain negative local results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Length-32 and length-80 inputs both use the same training N.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21405">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21405-mobius-rope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8f3ab0c1ff95aa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ms-gla" data-paper-title="MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ms-gla-a1875a93" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-95933f677c9061f9">Why give MS-GLA heads different temporal scales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ams-gla">MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One resolution can bottleneck representations. Some heads preserve token-level variation, others use pooled history, and their outputs combine.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Phrase detail and trends across phrases can use different update rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.35664-ms-gla/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-95933f677c9061f9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ms-gla" data-paper-title="MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea64391758996402">How does MS-GLA avoid leaking later tokens when pooling a block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ams-gla">MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each coarse branch masked-averages nonoverlapping blocks and runs GLA. A summary becomes visible only at the block end; causal hold restores token resolution without broadcasting into earlier positions. Input-conditioned weights fuse scales.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>In a four-token block, position two cannot see the average including positions three and four.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.35664-ms-gla/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea64391758996402">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ms-gla" data-paper-title="MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d3d6b392df03331">Why is multiscale GLA more than a larger window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ams-gla">MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each scale pools at a different nonoverlapping granularity before GLA, changing temporal update resolution. Extending a window still updates at the original rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating once per four words differs from updating every word while looking farther back.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.35664-ms-gla/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d3d6b392df03331">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ms-gla" data-paper-title="MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-97483a5c9b1dce32">When may tokens access scale-four pooled state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ams-gla">MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At or after the block&#x27;s final token. Use causal hold and input softmax fusion rather than broadcasting full means to every token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Token one cannot use the average of words one through four before word four arrives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.35664-ms-gla/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97483a5c9b1dce32">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:naju" data-paper-title="Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-naju-616fb3d6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5585d4a9b7fbb306">Why independently control old-state retention and new writes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anaju">Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared complementary gate creates a tradeoff. Separate retain/write gates in the discrete transition let both adjust independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading an important new fact need not erase an old fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21000-naju/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5585d4a9b7fbb306">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:naju" data-paper-title="Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e4296cda59e007b">Why separate retention and writing rather than use complementary gates in Naju?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anaju">Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A complementary write would shrink whenever retention is strong. Independent gates on native discrete dynamics can preserve old state and write new evidence together. Token-dependent directions, convolution, and feedthrough still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep a name while adding age instead of erasing the name in proportion to the new write.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21000-naju/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e4296cda59e007b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:naju" data-paper-title="Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e36079e843449dc1">How do Naju&#x27;s native discrete poles differ from Mamba discretizing continuous dynamics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anaju">Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Naju directly parameterizes discrete retention. Mamba derives a transition from continuous dynamics and input-dependent time steps. Both recur but formulas and gate coupling differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One learns the retained fraction per step directly; the other derives it from a time step and continuous matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21000-naju/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e36079e843449dc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:naju" data-paper-title="Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5b9b10c234e61db">How should preserve-first initialization set Naju&#x27;s two gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anaju">Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>forget_bias=5 and write_bias=−2 create strong initial retention and weak writes. Retain token-dependent B/C and direct feedthrough.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sigmoid(5)≈0.993 and sigmoid(−2)≈0.119 are not equal gates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21000-naju/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5b9b10c234e61db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:native-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-native-sparse-attention-6720d24e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-564f44b322bba736">Why use compression, selection, and window paths together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anative-sparse-attention">Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They provide global overview, exact selected detail, and exact recent context, respectively. Learned gates combine them; one sparsity pattern need not serve all roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Get topic summary, a distant key sentence, and current phrase detail from different paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-564f44b322bba736">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:native-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f731030c47e87c33">Why retain original blocks and a sliding window in addition to compressed NSA history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anative-sparse-attention">Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compression gives cheap global context but can lose details. Query-selected original blocks recover precise evidence, and a window covers recent tokens. All three paths learn and fuse from pretraining and remain causal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A summary can identify the chapter about dates; exact selected tokens resolve the year and the window preserves current qualifiers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f731030c47e87c33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:native-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a405b8a8da3af38e">How does NSA differ from pruning low attention weights after training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anative-sparse-attention">Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Three paths and their gates are trained jointly from pretraining, changing what the model learns to access. Post-hoc deletion from a dense model does not provide the same adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The model learns to trade summary and detailed blocks rather than suddenly losing history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a405b8a8da3af38e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:native-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f9175d8e49ec4071">Do all three NSA branches need causal boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anative-sparse-attention">Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Compressed blocks, selected fine blocks, and windows cannot expose future information. Align output dimensions before gated fusion. Local edge counts do not measure paper Triton throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mask future words in a selected block spanning the query position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f9175d8e49ec4071">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oal" data-paper-title="Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-oal-9fb61fc3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e990ea924ac5ed7a">Why focus on high-contribution post-RoPE QK coordinates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoal">Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coordinate contributions are uneven; a high-contribution tail can dominate error. Grouping and positive quadratic kernels target these differences rather than treating every coordinate alike.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A few coordinates driving most score changes merit different approximation from low-contribution ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13674-oal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e990ea924ac5ed7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oal" data-paper-title="Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ef7344fcef7af22">Why group QK contribution dimensions and calibrate OAL against output error?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoal">Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A few coordinates can dominate softmax approximation error. OAL finds stable post-RoPE groups and learns positive-definite quadratic kernels for shared groups and pairs. Vectors after aggregation, not only weights, reveal impact; positivity protects normalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal weight errors have different effects if one location has a large or very different value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13674-oal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ef7344fcef7af22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oal" data-paper-title="Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b02978e4ca43559d">How does OAL output MSE differ from fitting attention weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoal">Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Output depends on values and normalized aggregation, so equal weight errors can affect outputs differently. Calibrate the kernel to actual readouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping weights on identical values changes nothing, unlike swapping opposite values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13674-oal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b02978e4ca43559d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oal" data-paper-title="Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb26be760a2e1b53">Which OAL grouping, calibration, and initialization choices may use test data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoal">Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>None. Train supports grouping, calibration, and LoRA; validation selects initialization and checkpoint; test comes last. Keep ε in the positive kernel to ensure a positive denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not replace the validation-selected kernel with one found better on test and report that same test again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13674-oal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb26be760a2e1b53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oda" data-paper-title="On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-oda-5fd8c6ed" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-edf84b3436ce3886">Are ODA local and remote history divided by importance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoda">On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southern University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They describe distance relative to the current token. Relevant evidence can be far and nearby words irrelevant, motivating optional global reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A name at the document start can be critical outside the current window.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.20734-oda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edf84b3436ce3886">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oda" data-paper-title="On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-63a2a877c0ad9062">When does On-Demand Attention trigger global retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoda">On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southern University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A cheap recall head predicts benefit before expensive global attention and triggers it only for worthwhile tokens. Full KV stays stored; it saves some reads, not cache capacity. Misses can hide relevant distant evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Punctuation may use local context, while quoting an opening number triggers global reading; decide before paying for it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.20734-oda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63a2a877c0ad9062">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oda" data-paper-title="On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-88cec963475ac414">How does on-demand retrieval differ from evicting old KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoda">On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southern University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ODA retains all KV and varies when it is read. Eviction removes historical entries from the accessible set and changes memory capacity as well.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token skipped now may still be retrieved next step if retained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.20734-oda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88cec963475ac414">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oda" data-paper-title="On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f3461a49801c34b">Why must ODA decide before computing global attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoda">On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southern University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Computing global attention first already pays the cost. The gate must control conditional execution. A local A100 receipt verifies the path, not end-to-end vLLM throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading the whole book before choosing the contents page saves no reading.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.20734-oda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f3461a49801c34b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:olmpool-long-context" data-paper-title="Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-olmpool-long-context-26415a28" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c86c25ddeee07a58">Why use a controlled OLMpool model pool?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aolmpool-long-context">Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ai2</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real models often differ in normalization, GQA, training length, and sliding windows simultaneously. The pool isolates these choices and their combinations for long-context extension.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If architecture and training length both change, do not attribute the result to one toggle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10296-olmpool-long-context/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c86c25ddeee07a58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:olmpool-long-context" data-paper-title="Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-43e1a94b62bc3646">Why isn&#x27;t matching parameter count sufficient for comparing long-context methods?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aolmpool-long-context">Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ai2</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalization, GQA, pretraining windows, and sliding attention can all change long-context behavior. A controlled model pool isolates them; one model&#x27;s success does not generalize a positional or attention modification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A longer-pretrained model beating a shorter-trained model does not isolate the extension method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10296-olmpool-long-context/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43e1a94b62bc3646">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:olmpool-long-context" data-paper-title="Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa900f1f7e8c421c">How does changing normalization within the pool differ from comparing released models?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aolmpool-long-context">Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ai2</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Released models can also differ in data, scale, and schedule. Controlled changes improve attribution, and interactions mean single-factor effects need not add.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swap normalization alone, then test whether the direction persists with GQA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10296-olmpool-long-context/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa900f1f7e8c421c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:olmpool-long-context" data-paper-title="Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-31598daf655929d5">Does a passing local mini-suite establish the 7B pool&#x27;s conclusions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aolmpool-long-context">Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ai2</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It verifies core data flow, not paper-scale checkpoints or full benchmarks. Causal attribution needs controlled training, matched extension protocols, and task evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accuracy on 64 diagnostic examples is not a controlled 7B long-context experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10296-olmpool-long-context/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31598daf655929d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:openattention" data-paper-title="OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-openattention-57f03e45" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6de51fcd1292a9c7">Why not read only a few important KV entries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopenattention">OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sogang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A low read rate can leave substantial total mass in the tail. Counted residual-cluster averages supplement exact reads instead of treating the tail as zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many individually weak tokens can jointly affect the output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30951v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6de51fcd1292a9c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:openattention" data-paper-title="OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-deccca2f42b3b93c">Why use a count-weighted proxy for unread KV in OpenAttention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopenattention">OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sogang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-k discards all unread softmax mass. Query-relevant geometry groups tokens, with more exact reads where estimated error is high. Residual mean keys/values enter joint normalization with log counts. This preserves approximate mass, not exact attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A mean proxy for 100 similar tail tokens needs count correction or it represents just one entry.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30951v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-deccca2f42b3b93c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:openattention" data-paper-title="OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b733e66f95bcc284">What does a residual proxy retain beyond ordinary top-k?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopenattention">OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sogang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The residual mean and count approximate omitted contributions and share softmax with exact tokens. The mean is not exact recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A proxy for 100 remaining tokens should not participate with single-token mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30951v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b733e66f95bcc284">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:openattention" data-paper-title="OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-72235cc045539e99">Why recompute cluster residuals after selecting exact tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopenattention">OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sogang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise exact rows are counted twice. Remove them, recompute means and counts, add log count to logits, and omit empty clusters. Keep documented deterministic boundaries rather than heuristic fixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting three of ten leaves a seven-item proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30951v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72235cc045539e99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:orthros" data-paper-title="Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-orthros-ce7b4e60" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c10d95f900154d7">Why separate base and output-specific tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aorthros">Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Most prefill positions build cache rather than emit outputs. Base uses a fixed window and retains full KV; output-specific queries read it when predictions are needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Most prompt positions in a long document need not perform global output reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13735-orthros/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c10d95f900154d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:orthros" data-paper-title="Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d753314406f18da1">How can Orthros decode from all history after local prefill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aorthros">Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Base tokens use sliding attention but build full per-layer KV. Output-specific queries read shared full history where predictions are required and do not write KV. Fixed-window prefill compute is linear, not linear-attention state or reduced cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>During prefill base tokens read neighbors, while the final output query and future decode positions can retrieve full stored history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13735-orthros/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d753314406f18da1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:orthros" data-paper-title="Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8cd696712fa94f4">Is Orthros linear prefill kernelized linear attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aorthros">Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed-window SWA costs O(Tw). The output stream still performs ordinary causal cross-attention over full KV; it neither compresses into recurrence nor discards old cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>KV at the start remains available even if most prompt positions never read it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13735-orthros/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8cd696712fa94f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:orthros" data-paper-title="Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7da10ef89316529a">Should Orthros&#x27;s output stream append its own K/V?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aorthros">Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Same-layer KV comes only from base. Output queries use a shared projection and stream-specific affine transforms. Writing output KV changes the contract and may break cached-versus-batch parity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Append one base KV per step, not one per stream.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13735-orthros/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7da10ef89316529a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rea" data-paper-title="Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rea-ef53c923" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d6cddee4d267173">Why not top-k system instructions with chat history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Area">Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
