<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global instructions persist across turns. Episodic content is retrieved separately and handled by role.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lasting formatting requirement should not be evicted for low similarity to the current query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00958-rea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d6cddee4d267173">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rea" data-paper-title="Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-958b8fd9fb9bf5ff">Why keep global instructions in a persistent REA prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Area">Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relevance ranking should not discard standing constraints. REA separates them from episodic retrieval, which applies role-specific preservation, compression, or omission. Context selection is not lossless reconstruction; policies require verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A standing Chinese-output requirement must not disappear during a movie discussion merely for low keyword similarity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00958-rea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-958b8fd9fb9bf5ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rea" data-paper-title="Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d014abe718e687fc">How does role-aware episodic retrieval differ from a recent window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Area">Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It can retrieve distant relevant interactions instead of using recency alone, and retains persistent instructions independently. Role policies treat content differently; compression may lose information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recover an older preference while dropping recent irrelevant tool logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00958-rea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d014abe718e687fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rea" data-paper-title="Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-155fe90c15fcfee8">Does the local REA top-k path include real LLM compression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Area">Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It executes role separation and episodic retrieval without a compression LLM. Distinguish selection from generated summaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing three passages does not show an LM compressed them faithfully.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00958-rea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-155fe90c15fcfee8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rope" data-paper-title="RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rope-baa4b020" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-821e31f5f271e6be">Why rotate two-dimensional Q/K subspaces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arope">RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhuiyi Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Position determines rotation angle, so dot products depend on relative phase and content without learning one vector per position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical content at distances 2 and 20 can produce different scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09864">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-821e31f5f271e6be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rope" data-paper-title="RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9430b8ac22a0b9f9">Why do absolute Q/K rotations yield relative position in RoPE dot products?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arope">RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhuiyi Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The first rotation&#x27;s transpose cancels the shared absolute phase, leaving displacement n−m. Q/K subspaces rotate, not values. Evaluability at larger positions does not guarantee trained retrieval extrapolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving positions 3 and 8 to 13 and 18 preserves distance 5 and their relative phase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09864">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9430b8ac22a0b9f9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rope" data-paper-title="RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-22c3fb74dae17ab4">How does RoPE differ from adding absolute embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arope">RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhuiyi Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Absolute embeddings modify representations additively. RoPE rotates Q/K so the inner product can express a relative rotation. These are different operations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shifting both segments equally preserves RoPE&#x27;s relative phase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09864">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22c3fb74dae17ab4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rope" data-paper-title="RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcc3c0bb705d3c12">Can RoPE rotate only Q or only K?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arope">RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhuiyi Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Relative displacement requires both R_m and R_n. Pair channels correctly and continue absolute positions through incremental decode.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A single input token at position 100 still uses rotation 100, not zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09864">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcc3c0bb705d3c12">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sas-attention" data-paper-title="SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-sas-attention-90d42e99" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8e073aa1cf873934">Why keep continuous SAS gates rather than only selected indices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asas-attention">SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent HY LLM Frontier / HKUST (Guangzhou) / HKUST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The integer indices choose blocks but do not carry gradients. Gates in attention let prediction loss train selection scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical selected blocks with 0.8/0.2 versus 0.5/0.5 produce different outputs and gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13141">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.13141-sas-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8e073aa1cf873934">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sas-attention" data-paper-title="SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6b2dc7c35d29a0f">How does SAS train its selector despite nondifferentiable top-k indices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asas-attention">SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent HY LLM Frontier / HKUST (Guangzhou) / HKUST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It preserves continuous gates for selected blocks and adds log gates inside attention softmax. LM loss differentiates through gate values, not indices. History gates normalize jointly and the current block stays at one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing two selected gates from 0.8/0.2 to 0.6/0.4 changes output and gradients without changing indices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13141">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.13141-sas-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6b2dc7c35d29a0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sas-attention" data-paper-title="SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fdfbe025d1dba3e">How does LM-loss selector training differ from distilling dense attention rankings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asas-attention">SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent HY LLM Frontier / HKUST (Guangzhou) / HKUST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token prediction provides task feedback rather than supervising imitation of dense attention. It needs continuous gates; hard top-k remains nondifferentiable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A block ranked highly by the dense model need not contribute equally to prediction loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13141">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.13141-sas-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fdfbe025d1dba3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sas-attention" data-paper-title="SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d9c14bab0803e99">Where does SAS add the log gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asas-attention">SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent HY LLM Frontier / HKUST (Guangzhou) / HKUST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Add log gates for selected history to attention logits before shared softmax. Normalize history gates together and set current block to one. Post-output scaling changes the normalization relationship.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Current gate one adds zero; history blocks compete with their respective log gates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13141">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.13141-sas-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d9c14bab0803e99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stratified-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-stratified-sparse-attention-869759f6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e03b2497b28be11">Why retain heavy entries deterministically and sample the tail?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astratified-sparse-attention">Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rice University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-k drops the tail; uniform sampling can waste budget. SSA uses proxy scores to divide deterministic and residual budgets, then corrects by inclusion probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strong evidence remains while weaker entries have a chance of inclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28441v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28441-stratified-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e03b2497b28be11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stratified-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-80e8ff6ac2401e91">Why correct by the probability of at least one draw after deduplicating SSA samples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astratified-sparse-attention">Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rice University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A repeated token appears only once in the set, so inclusion is 1−(1−p)^m rather than single-draw p. Deterministically retained heavy items have inclusion one. The final self-normalized ratio is not strictly unbiased.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At p=0.2 and two draws, weight one retained row using 0.36, not 0.2.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28441v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28441-stratified-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80e8ff6ac2401e91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stratified-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-53b2ad3285caf307">Why not correct deduplicated with-replacement samples by 1/p_i?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astratified-sparse-attention">Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rice University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each token enters once with π_i=1−(1−p_i)^m. Divide by inclusion, not per-draw probability. The self-normalized numerator/denominator ratio still need not be unbiased.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token drawn three times but retained once is not three independent weighted observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28441v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28441-stratified-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53b2ad3285caf307">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stratified-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04c938ddcf6c6174">How does SSA compute small inclusion probabilities and test full budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astratified-sparse-attention">Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rice University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use −expm1(m·log1p(−p)) and log-space normalization for stability. Return dense attention explicitly at k=N. Detached discrete allocation is not a gradient path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A budget of all keys must match dense output without randomly losing tail tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28441v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28441-stratified-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04c938ddcf6c6174">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-attention" data-paper-title="Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-switch-attention-753b5e50" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3235ac51ae30aba8">What can Switch Attention&#x27;s local and full paths read?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-attention">Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local reads the visible window; full reads all causal history, never the future. The router trades evidence range and compute per token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A nearby phrase may need only local context, while an old fact needs a wider read.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.26380-switch-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3235ac51ae30aba8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-attention" data-paper-title="Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-145fabe3734e92b3">Does Switch Attention choose one path per layer or per token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-attention">Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fine-grained router chooses full or local for each token. Training must account for discrete selection; actual savings depend on global call rate and overhead, and sparsity does not guarantee quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Nearby conjunctions can use local reads, while citing an early name may need global history in the same layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.26380-switch-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-145fabe3734e92b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-attention" data-paper-title="Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-31c3a79c4cb08720">How does hard switching differ from continuously mixing both branches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-attention">Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard selection can execute only one branch. Continuous mixing generally computes both and weights outputs. Gradients and savings differ; the local soft router is not the paper&#x27;s STE hard router.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiplying an already computed attention output by nearly zero does not save its execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.26380-switch-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31c3a79c4cb08720">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-attention" data-paper-title="Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1652841be38828b4">Can the local soft router demonstrate a branch-selective kernel speedup?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-attention">Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks mixing without hard routing, 32K continued pretraining, or fused selective kernels. Verify actual executed branches and runtime separately from gate values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 90% local weight does not prove 90% of global calls were skipped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.26380-switch-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1652841be38828b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:transmem" data-paper-title="TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-transmem-2625c67f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-27cc9d050984c6eb">Does a frozen TransMem backbone mean nothing learns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atransmem">TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The backbone stays fixed but evidence-conditioned self-distillation trains memory gating. Changing memory is not updating backbone weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new branch can learn when to inject history into the current state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29032-transmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27cc9d050984c6eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:transmem" data-paper-title="TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-322b52536e46b91b">How does parameter memory from hidden states differ from retaining original history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atransmem">TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TransMem converts sparse states from a frozen backbone to reusable gated deltas. It avoids re-reading the same original tokens but trades reuse for detail lost in selection/compression. Learned gating does not retrain the backbone per history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A compressed document can support later queries without recovering an omitted exact ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29032-transmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-322b52536e46b91b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:transmem" data-paper-title="TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb5007a2cbb3c70f">How does parameter memory differ from appending old text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atransmem">TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>T(H_sparse) transforms selected states into hidden-state updates, while text concatenation re-reads original tokens. This changes storage and fusion, and omitted detail may be lost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keeping a fact representation does not reproduce every omitted word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29032-transmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb5007a2cbb3c70f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:transmem" data-paper-title="TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-219e33d6432ab044">Should TransMem replace the original hidden state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atransmem">TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. h′=h+g⊙T(H_sparse) preserves the main path. Keep selection, transformation, and gated injection distinct. The mini-suite is not paper-scale training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With g=0, output is h rather than zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29032-transmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-219e33d6432ab044">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:triadic-linear-attention" data-paper-title="Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-triadic-linear-attention-debbb585" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c44e1dc920136d0b">Is linear-attention state a history list or accumulated associative memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atriadic-linear-attention">Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It accumulates key/value outer products into a matrix queried by contraction. Triadic adds another key axis, not a raw per-token KV list.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiple writes combine in a table with an added address dimension.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36529">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.36529-triadic-linear-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c44e1dc920136d0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:triadic-linear-attention" data-paper-title="Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d8ba49e4e0aa0df">How does a second key change Triadic Linear Attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atriadic-linear-attention">Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It adds an independently addressed key axis to ordinary key–value state and contracts with two queries. Capacity grows with that dimension, not for free. E=1 should recover ordinary linear attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A person&#x27;s value can depend on the scene as a second address, at the cost of a larger joint state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36529">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.36529-triadic-linear-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d8ba49e4e0aa0df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:triadic-linear-attention" data-paper-title="Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d494a0dcffab28cd">How is a second key axis different from widening values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atriadic-linear-attention">Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dimension E increases state capacity by E and enables an independent query contraction. Wider values add output content but not dual-key addressing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding more fields to records is different from adding a search key.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36529">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.36529-triadic-linear-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d494a0dcffab28cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:triadic-linear-attention" data-paper-title="Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a38956b9ce3cc27d">Why test the E=1 limit instead of merely checking forward execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atriadic-linear-attention">Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It must exactly reduce to ordinary linear attention, testing construction and contraction of the extra axis. Also compare explicit history sums, causality, and gradients; this is not long-book language quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Remove the second key&#x27;s freedom and match the same-input two-dimensional reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttcd" data-paper-title="Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ttcd-fe56ef12" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9888956d6e16b230">What information differs between teacher and student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attcd">Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher sees longer history, while student relies on its window or fast weights. Hidden-state targets teach retention without giving deployed students full history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher reads background; deployment still uses finite learned memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01672-ttcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9888956d6e16b230">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttcd" data-paper-title="Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-62897b0d29fdf49d">What does a short-window TTCD student learn beyond final answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attcd">Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long-window teacher hidden states supervise fast weights to retain context useful for future predictions. The student must select information under finite memory, not uniformly preserve every token. State distillation is not lossless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Store an early variable definition in fast weights to match later teacher state, rather than memorizing one answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01672-ttcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62897b0d29fdf49d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttcd" data-paper-title="Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e538a1608b476d1">What does state distillation constrain beyond final token matching?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attcd">Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It aligns intermediate teacher and student representations to train memory, not just output probabilities. Supervision location and space differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two students can predict the same token while retaining different historical information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01672-ttcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e538a1608b476d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttcd" data-paper-title="Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7295b9f8ace3f89d">Why align teacher and student positions and representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attcd">Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden loss compares the same t with compatible dimensions. Offsets or accidental broadcasting optimize the wrong target. Local results are not paper-scale long-context validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student step 20 aligns to teacher step 20, not the final document state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01672-ttcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7295b9f8ace3f89d">Question link</a></p>
